utterances.text: So if we follow the same logic now, in wartime, the police force must be resubordinated to the army and Territorial Defence because waging war and defence fall under the jurisdiction of the army and the Territorial Defence who are trained for that. Is that the prevailing logic?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, and I would like to add this. That this applies to wartime; whereas everything else that you said still stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: General, in your report -- now my colleague is telling me that what you said about combat operations hasn't been interpreted. Can you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, with your observation, and I would be more precise by adding that in wartime and during combat operation. As for everything else, it remains and is consistent with what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So, you said this a number of times, and that is, that the police is not trained and qualified to participate in war as an armed force.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To take part in combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Their participation in combat operations, based on the principle of resubordination of which you discussed extensively, should be an example rather than a rule; is that correct -- should be an exception rather than a rule.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That would be in compliance with the federal regulations and the republican regulations. In other words, in 1992, the police was not part of the armed forces of the Republika Srpska, nor was it part of the armed forces of ex-Yugoslavia; is that correct? The police force was not part of the armed force.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: However, sir, in your report, in paragraph 57, you state that in 1994 a change occurred. The police units became part of the armed forces of Republika Srpska and appropriate regulations were adopted to that end. Is that what your paragraph 57 say?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: General, you expressed your own reservation vis-a-vis the decision of competent authorities of Republika Srpska in terms of being authorised to adopt these kind of regulations by abiding -- by abiding by the principle that the police was not trained to carry out this kind of tasks.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was not a usual occurrence for police forces to be part of armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you discussed this, we haven't seen this particular regulation from 1994, and I think it would be helpful if we look at it so that we can see in what way the police was incorporated into the armed forces, and this has to do with the principles that we discussed. And, for that purpose, we need a document which is in our law library, and that's L317.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at page 2 in the Serbian and page 3 in English. Can we zoom in on Article 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And, General, it's your tab 7 in your binder so you may find it easier to read from the hard copy. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is the Law on the Implementation of the Law on In case of an imminent threat of war or a state of war. And, indeed, in Article 2, it is said exactly as you commented, i.e., that units of the Ministry of the Interior shall become part of the armed forces. Is that what is directly stemming from this article?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 4 in the Serbian version of this same document, and page 9 of the English version. We need Article 4. Can we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: General, have you managed to read the article? If not, can you please read it out loud. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the amendment to the Law on National Defence is accompanied by appropriate amendment to -- to the Law on the Interior, and it is now provided in detail how units of the interior shall become a part of the armed forces. General, in principle or, rather, let's say that the basic principle remains unchanged. The Supreme Commander remained in command of the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The principle of singleness of authority remains in place because the president of the republic is the Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move now to page 5 in the Serbian version and page 12 in the English version. We need Article 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read it carefully and in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I quote Article 4 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, read it to yourself?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, General, if you read it carefully none of the principles that we discussed was changed: The singleness, the resubordination, and --

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I would add to this, singleness of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So even when officially and legally the police force became a part of the armed forces, they are participating on the basis of the principle of resubordination to the army and are integrated into the system of military units, based on the principle of subordination and the execution of commands issued by military commanders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: General, if we read Article 14 carefully, it seems that the legislature's intention was only to regulate the participation of police in combat operations only when it is resubordinated. They wanted to introduce a certain order in that system, rather than to turn it into a -- an armed force, because we see that basically nothing has been changed.

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do we also agree that all these principles are obviously older than the law itself?

utterances.speaker: VIDOSAV KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to move onto another topic so if that is not a problem, we can finish a bit earlier. I planned my examination with regard to Ms. Korner's need for some time toward the end. But if you so prefer, I can also continue for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: How much longer do you expect you would be, Mr. Cvijetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm certain that I will finish tomorrow by the end of the first session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And are you telling us that you can't usefully make use of the next 19 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you insist, I can begin. I -- my proposal was only to stop now because I am about to deal with a completely different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, perhaps notwithstanding what I indicated at the beginning of this session, if it's the better use of time we could go back to what we originally planned and deal with this map situation. If that's convenient, Ms. Korner, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it's what we originally suggested, Your Honour. But I fail to see how Mr. Cvijetic could have planned his cross-examination on the basis that he was going to stop ten minutes, as we never suggested it until we way into morning. However, Your Honours, as I said I'm happy to deal with it whenever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we -- we would do that. General, you would have gathered from what has just passed between the Bench and counsel that we have certain procedural matters with which to deal and therefore we would excuse you a little early today, and -- so the usher would escort you from the courtroom now but we ourselves would not be rising immediately. So we would continue your cross-examination by Mr. Cvijetic tomorrow, and I believe we're back in Courtroom II tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the witness is asking whether he can take the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but the witness is asking whether he can take this document with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, do you have a problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I have no doubt he looked at them with Mr. Cvijetic when Mr. Cvijetic spoke to him in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before -- before we get to the maps, it's perhaps a good moment to remind the parties of the Andan document that they will have received by now. And ask for the parties' submissions on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Hannis who dealt with this witness, as far as -- as far as the Office of the Prosecutor is concerned, is proposing to ask that it be admitted. It's apparently an identical copy of another document that is already an exhibit but without the signatures or something like that. So that there's no translation needed but I thought we would leave that to Mr. Hannis to deal with it. I don't know what the Defence want to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is precisely the case. The witness testified that is he in possession of the identical document but without the signature and then he was requested -- there was a request and the order by the Trial Chamber that he provides that document. As far as I can see, it's the identical as the document that we have exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And you agree with Ms. Korner speaking for Mr. Hannis that it -- the document should be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if -- if it pleases the Court. I don't see any particular reason why it should be admitted. Because it's the original document -- it's the -- it's the identical copy of the document which is already an exhibit. Only without the signature. But if it pleases the Court, we do not object this document be exhibited also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I have no problem, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, if we have two identical documents, one with and one without signatures and stamps why should we admit also the one that is without anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I haven't the faintest idea, Your Honours, because I don't remember the first thing about the evidence of Mr. Andan. But I know that Mr. Hannis thinks there is a point. I believe it's to support his credibility. I discussed it -- I'm being given information. I think, Your Honours -- I've been given information, but I think it would be better if Mr. Hannis makes the submissions himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could the document be given a -- an exhibit number, the same exhibit number as the -- the signed one but with a decimal number, .1.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Then this would be P2349.1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. I know Mr. Hannis will be delighted. Your Honours, can I just very briefly tell Your Honours what -- do Your Honours have the binder here with the ethnic maps? There are 19 in total. Admitted so far out of the 19 are 9. I want the other 10, please, admitted. I don't know how we failed to notice that we haven't had them all admitted but there is no rhyme or reason to it. And that's our application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, can I just make sure that the one that we're speaking of is dated 2010 down at the right-hand side of the cover page, at the bottom? We have two --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's right. It starts with 1, Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina and ends, 19, Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the one. And, Your Honours, if necessary, I can give you the ones which are already admitted, and the ones that aren't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zecevic, could we hear the basis on which you have a difficulty with this application.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We do object to this admittance of these ethnic maps, and the -- and the time of admission, if I may say so, proposed by Ms. Korner. Namely, Your Honours, on page 15216, the matter was raised for the first time with Your Honours on the 1st of October 2010. And Your Honour, Judge Hall, said, on -- when Ms. Pidwell was approaching the Trial Chamber concerning this map and Your Honour stated: [As read] "My recollection is that the pieces of it have migrated into the trial as separate exhibits. So consistent with that, I suppose we would exhibit this page." On the 21st of October, 2010, page -- transcript page 16333, Ms. Korner was, again, raising the matter. And Your Honours said: [As read] "It was pointed out to me" - Your Honour, Judge Hall - "but it was pointed out to me that from the time we would have started, separate pages have been individually exhibited and I --" And Ms. Korner then says yes. And Your Honour says: "And I having started out down that path, we must continue." Therefore, the -- the -- the -- the decision of the Trial Chamber was that each and every ethnical map will be separately introduced in the exhibit. At that point Ms. Korner says: [As read] "Well, I think probably the answer is, Your Honour, when we file the bar table motion, if we can just throw in the maps that have already -- that have not already been exhibited as part of that and rather than starting to work out which ones are in and which ones aren't yet." Therefore, Your Honours, at the very least on two occasions which I could find in the transcript the matter was raised. The Office of the Prosecutor said that they would offer them -- these maps as a part of their bar table motion and they haven't. In the meantime, they closed their case and now they want to introduce these maps during the -- the -- the Zupljanin case, after Stanisic case was closed. Your Honours, if -- if Ms. Korner would have done what she proposed to do, namely, to offer these documents as -- as part of the -- the bar table motion, I would have explained, to the very detail, why I object and why I say these ethnic maps are completely unreliable. I made -- I made a reference to that on -- on the 1st of September, 2010, transcript page 14029 to 14032, when I tried to explain why precisely after one of the witnesses was actually questioning the -- the -- the accuracy of these maps or didn't accept what was proposed and what was stated in this map as accurate. And then we had the argument, and I -- and I explained why I think these maps are unreliable. And I am prepared to give, if Your Honours, I'm prepared to give my reasons why I -- why I say so, that the maps unreliable if Your Honours will permit to do that at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Perhaps you would like to read Judge Hall's response to your objection as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, thank you very much but I think you will have the opportunity to address the Court at the proper time. And then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Since we're at this point, can you remind me as to what my response was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which objection Ms. Korner is [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... There was only -- Your Honour, there was one objection, which was never raised again, at that stage about the accuracy of these maps and when it was raised by Mr. Zecevic, Your Honour Judge Hall said: [As read] "Mr. Zecevic, save for maps which are confined to showing geographical features, all maps could probably be criticised as being politically biased in some way or other and it seems to me that, save for counsel giving evidence, which at one point I thought you were in danger of doing, the problem, which the OTP probably accepts, is cured. If cured, it could be by the oral testimony they just elicited from the witness. So in other words the Chambers would have the map and to the extent there are any flaws the Chamber would then have to look at it alongside the explanation given by this witness or any other witness." Your Honours, if you look at the maps, you will see that they repeat the statistics, which are not disputed, of the ethnic breakdown of the municipalities. They also show in -- in -- in colour form, the rough, and it is accepted you can't be entirely accurate, breakdown of each of the villages shown on the map. It is not, in our submission, a question of admissibility. Your Honours have admitted them in each case. It's a question of weight. And, as I say, the statistics which are given at the top are undisputed in this case. They come from the census held in 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Ms. Korner. Mr. Zecevic, what I was -- my inclination is this. First of all, do I appreciate that your objection is two-fold. One, is the time; and, secondly, is the reliability -- whatever is -- it seems to me that in terms of the matter of reliability, as Ms. Korner has reminded us the view of the chamber was that this is a matter for argumentation. It is it inevitable there is controversy in that regard. So it would be a question of weight. But in terms of the other question it seems to me that this rides alongside a motion which the -- I don't know if it's a motion but there is a matter which the Chamber now has under consideration and that is about death certificates. And the Chamber is -- has that under active consideration so could we, inasmuch as the reasoning would be identical, should we wait until we have decided the -- what, in our view, is the correct answer to that issue, and the -- your objection about timing would then be solved or not solved by that decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You're precisely correct, Your Honours. I do believe that this -- the way how -- how the Office of the Prosecutor tried to -- to -- or requested that these documents be admitted is actually a motion to reopen their case and therefore it is quite similar to the issue of the death charts, which -- and I agree that the most sensible way would be to -- to -- to decide on both matters simultaneously when the Trial Chamber is deciding on -- on the proper motion which was made by -- by the Office of the Prosecutor concerning the death charts. But concerning the reliability of this -- these documents, what I was trying to say, Your Honours, is that there is one slight point which I would like to raise. In -- I do agree with Your Honours that it goes to the weight, but in this precise case, where we had the witness who says, This map is not accurate, this map is wrong, then -- then it is possible for Your Honours and everybody else to assess the weight of -- of that particular map. And that is precisely why these maps should -- should be tendered through the witnesses. In this occasion, we will not have any witness to confirm or to challenge the accuracy of that map. And I stay with what I said, despite what Ms. Korner is saying, that these maps are -- are not reliable and that -- that they were produced by one of the parties to the conflict in the former Yugoslavia for a specific purpose. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] add something else. It's not quite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] May I have a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just say one thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, it appears to us that this matter is not as easily resolved as we first thought it would be, and we think that procedurally, the Prosecution should file a motion, whether it's a supplement to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... But, Your Honour, it's not the same. That's what I was about to say. I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, but just very quickly, because I know you've got to rise. It's not the same category as the death certificates. It is not new evidence. They have all been there, they have all been used in one form or another. We forgot - there's no other word for it - when we were plowing through the MFI documents and the ones we hadn't gotten in, to add the maps as we said we would in the bar table motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I hear everything you have said, and may I respectfully suggest that you advise yourself as to what to call the motion that you would file.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think I will express my feelings to your legal officer after court. Your Honours, for that reason, if Your Honours prefer, we'll put it in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment to resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of September, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
